title: 4 people stop looking for work. Then?
hook: Nobody finds a job, but 4 people stop searching. What does the unemployment rate do?

knows: a rate is a part over a whole
doesNotKnow: that the unemployment rate counts only people looking for work, so when job-seekers stop looking the rate falls although nobody found a job

misconception: When the unemployment rate falls, more people have jobs.
objective: The learner can explain that when 4 of 10 job-seekers stop looking the rate falls from 10% to 6.25% with jobs unchanged at 90, almost the same as 4 finding jobs (6%, jobs 94), because people who stop looking leave both the top and the bottom of the fraction.

claims.text: In this count, the unemployment rate is people looking ÷ (people working + people looking); people not looking are not counted.
claims.source: Lesson rule stated on the stage chip (a definition the lesson sets). Brief: company/domains/briefs/economics.md #62 keeps official definitions (ILO, BLS) and the term 'discouraged workers' out of learner text until a human source check passes.

claims.text: With 90 working and 10 looking the rate is 10%; when 4 of the 10 stop looking it is 6 / 96 = 6.25% and jobs stay at 90.
When 4 of the 10 find jobs instead, the rate is 6 / 100 = 6% and jobs rise to 94.
When people stop looking they leave the count, so the top and the bottom of the fraction both shrink; a falling rate alone cannot tell which case happened, the number of jobs can.
claims.source: From the rule in c1: a person moving from looking to not looking lowers numerator and denominator by 1; a person moving from looking to working lowers only the numerator. The two cases above give 6.25% vs 6% with jobs 90 vs 94.

claims.text: The lesson is a toy town of 100 people, not any country's statistics.

recall.question: A town's unemployment rate fell from 8% to 5% this year. What do you need to know before saying more people have jobs?
options: Nothing: a lower rate means more jobs
Whether the number of people working went up, or job-seekers just stopped looking
recall.why: The rate counts only people looking. If job-seekers stop looking they leave the count and the rate falls with no new jobs, so check the number of jobs.
